extracted.intended_audience: researchers and teacher-educators developing or using real-time classroom observation protocols to measure pedagogical content knowledge (PCK) in secondary mathematics
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and using a real-time classroom observation protocol to measure teachers' pedagogical content knowledge (curricular content, discourse, anticipatory, and implementation knowledge) in secondary mathematics lessons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curricular content knowledge (CCK)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Curricular content knowledge is substantive knowledge about topics, procedures, and concepts along with a comprehension of the relationships among them as they are offered in school curricula’ (p.2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Columns of the observation protocol are assigned loadings indicating whether a given observable category provides evidence of curricular content knowledge; CCK columns contribute to the CCK score when their loadings include a 1. Example: 'encourages diverse mathematical competencies' was assigned a CCK loading of 1 because the teacher must know the curriculum sufficiently to encourage competencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discourse knowledge (DK)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Discourse knowledge is substantive knowledge about the culturally embedded nature of inquiry and forms of communication in mathematics (both in and out of educational settings)’ and includes mathematical syntax as a sub-category (p.2). The authors adopt Gee’s broad notion of Discourses (ways of being) and treat discourse to include gestures, interactions, and connected stretches of language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Columns that load on DK tend to involve interactional/relational features between teacher and students. DK is dynamic and often overlaps heavily with other PCK components; changes in DK may drive changes in other components such as implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipatory knowledge (AK)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Anticipatory knowledge is an awareness of, and responsiveness to, the diverse ways in which learners may engage with content, processes, and concepts’ (p.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AK loadings are used to construct the AK score by summing columns that the research team determined provide evidence of anticipatory knowledge. AK can overlap with discourse and implementation; decreases in observed AK may reflect implementation dips or contextual factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation (action) knowledge (IK)
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Implementation or action knowledge includes knowledge about how to adapt teaching according to content and socio-cultural context and enact in the classroom the decisions informed by content, discourse, and anticipatory understandings’ (p.3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementation knowledge was operationalized to require both adaptation and enactment. Determining which observable categories indicate IK required team consensus because IK is deeply interwoven with the other PCK components.

rubrics_metrics.name: PA / PI / NPA / NPI coding scheme
rubrics_metrics.description: Each observation category is coded per 3-minute segment with one of four codes: Present and Appropriate (PA), Present and Inappropriate (PI), Not Present and Appropriate (NPA), Not Present and Inappropriate (NPI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring guidance: for aggregation the team assigns +1 for each PA, -1 for each PI or NPI, and 0 for each NPA. Example: a teacher’s response that does not address a student’s question and does not make sense to the student was coded NPI in the 'explicit talk about ways of reasoning' column and NPI in 'interprets students’ productions/student errors'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observation segment length and sampling cadence
rubrics_metrics.description: Use brief, repeated segments for real-time observation: observe for 3 minutes, then record for 3 minutes (a 3-minute on / 3-minute off cadence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: the original 5-on/5-off approach produced too few codings per class and was cognitively burdensome; the 3/3 cadence yields about 9 samples per 45–55-minute class (up to 15 in block periods), improving measurement density and feasibility of accurate real-time coding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Glossary / coding-book design
rubrics_metrics.description: Build a glossary (coding book) with explicit definitions, in vivo exemplars, examples and non-examples for each observation category to guide coders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The glossary should reduce ambiguity in terms like 'explicit' and 'inappropriate' and act as a coding book so that observers after brief calibration can apply codes consistently. Include exemplar segments from real lessons to illustrate coding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quadruplet loadings (c,d,a,i) for columns
rubrics_metrics.description: Each observation column is assigned a quadruplet (c, d, a, i) with values 1 or 0 indicating whether the category provides observable evidence of curricular content (c), discourse (d), anticipatory (a), or implementation (i) knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Loadings are determined by the research team through consensus. Some columns may have multiple 1s (indicating overlap) and some columns may have all zeros. The component (PCK) scores are computed by summing columns whose quadruplet has a 1 in the relevant component position.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring aggregation and norming procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Aggregate per-column tallies (PA/PI/NPA/NPI) across segments into a column total using +1 (PA), -1 (PI or NPI), and 0 (NPA); then norm column totals within an observation to account for varying numbers of segments. Compute each PCK component score by summing normed totals for columns that load on that component and average across observations for each teacher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This produces component-level scores (e.g., proportion-like means such as 'teachers demonstrated IK in 51.9% of segments'). Use statistical tests (paired t-tests, independent samples t-tests) to compare pre/post or between cohorts. Interpret cautiously: observed usage in segments ≠ total knowledge possession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'explicit talk about a topic or subject'
rubrics_metrics.description: Glossary definition used: any utterance from student or teacher in which a topic or subject is stated verbally or in writing or by reference to a clear written or verbal precursor familiar to people in the room (e.g., through gestures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide in vivo exemplars illustrating when such talk is present and when it is not. Use this definition when coding columns related to explicit talk or reasoning; the paper gives an example of coding a segment NPI when the teacher's reply did not address the student's question in a comprehensible way.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condensing and redefining LMT categories (e.g., multiple representations)
rubrics_metrics.description: When adapting LMT (2006) categories for secondary real-time observation, some categories were condensed (for example, selection of correct manipulatives and multiple models were condensed into a single 'multiple representations' column).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Condense categories where appropriate to make a streamlined, real-time tool (authors reduced LMT's 30+ categories to 20). Ensure condensed columns still capture the intent of original categories and document scope in the glossary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Column example: 'encourages diverse mathematical competencies' and its loadings
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'encourages diverse mathematical competencies' column was assigned a quadruplet of (1,0,1,1) indicating it loads on curricular content, anticipatory, and implementation knowledge but not discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanation: the teacher must know curriculum (CCK) to encourage competencies, must anticipate how students will interact (AK), adapt and enact instruction (IK), and will demonstrate some discourse during enactment. Document such rationale for each column's loadings to support reliability and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-rater reliability practices: paired recoding and calibration
rubrics_metrics.description: To improve inter-rater reliability the LMT team and this team recoded lessons in pairs and used a glossary; the current team recommends brief calibration training paired with a practiced observer or using shared video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because individual coders’ professional backgrounds cause variability, pair recoding and calibration reduce drift. The instrument should be terse but include sufficient examples so briefly trained coders can apply codes similarly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow for non-linearity and overlap among PCK components
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt a non-linear view of PCK: observable teacher moves can demonstrate multiple PCK facets simultaneously and categories should allow overlap rather than forcing orthogonal measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use loadings (quadruplets) and accept that column evidence may contribute to multiple component scores. The protocol and subsequent modeling should account for interdependence among components rather than assuming strict linear separability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instrument design principle: terse but sufficiently detailed for quick calibration
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal is an instrument 'that is terse but of sufficient detail that individuals can observe classrooms after a brief calibration training paired with a practiced observer or after watching video of the same.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance the number of columns (authors reduced to ~20) and the depth of glossary examples so real-time use is feasible without sacrificing inter-rater reliability; include vivid exemplars and non-examples to clarify borderline cases.
